reviews.title: A Buggy Masterpiece
reviews.text: Don’t let the low rating fool you, this app is genuinely amazing, I was on track to learning a new language fairly quickly thanks to how helpful and useful the app and programs are, however, one day all momentum came to a crashing halt when the app would no longer be able to pick up my voice for some odd reason. I thought maybe I was just really mispronouncing the phrase it wanted me to repeat back, so I went to an older lesson that I for sure knew, yet it still refused to work with me. I made sure Speech Recognition and the Microphone permissions were turned on, and to my surprise they were. It’s not an issue of the microphone on my end because I’m still able to call and record video properly so I’m just really bummed out I can no longer use the app. :(

reviews.title: Best language learning app I’ve ever used
reviews.text:
Teuida is the first language learning app that I am thoroughly impressed with. I’ve used Duolingo, Rosetta Stone, AirLearn, Memrise, and Pimsleur. I believe that Teuida’s approach to learning a language is better than anything else I’ve ever used. In my opinion, they have bypassed the major trap in learning a new language: translating in your head. You should be thinking in the language you are learning and not constantly using your mother tongue as a reference to form sentences. 

The plant streak idea is also a very amazing idea. You can see your consistency literally flourish and bloom. By far best language learning app I’ve ever used. Supplement this app with your own learning of the languages’ grammar and you are set!

reviews.title: Do it
reviews.text:
I’m nit picky with language learning because a lot of “resources” are trash, but I’ve used Teuida for Japanese and now Korean - and it’s genuinely my favorite. Especially because a lot of people will tell you the same thing, not being able to speak is a big challenge - so being able to repeat things out loud is incredibly helpful. 

Not just that, but unlike the garbage app with the bird, Teuida actually teaches you what you need to know. :)

reviews.title: Rough Process [learning korean]
reviews.text: They have an  ebook itself which is additional help with the units that breaks it down in words what the videos teach. BUT units contain inconsistencies and spelling errors! Starting Unit 11. And if you are not going back and forth between the book and app you will end up more confused. It’s more of a supplementary book than a complete book. AND takes forever to receive. There is hardly any interaction with the users too. UI to get around needs improvement too. The content ALL together is good but you will find yourself doing much more investigating than actually learning.
